goal: Make the stored preview dispatch instruction name its dispatch mode, so a write route cannot silently dry-run. The producer attaches mode_sequence to the ready record AFTER both digests are taken, deliberately leaving ready_id and manifest_digest unchanged; mode_sequence is carried for a later phase and no validator refuses a manifest that omits it today. Two things are enforced. The production gate's bare test -n checks gain named REFUSED messages instead of dying with only an exit code. And re-preparing a preview-ready identity written before this change still converges. Generation 3 attempted that second behaviour by narrowing the STORED digest to ready identity, which was wrong and was rejected by two independent reviews: consumers re-derive sha256(canonicalJson(<stored record>)) from the record they read back (manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:2094), so narrowing the writer repaired the 117 pre-change refs by making every NEWLY written ref unreadable and fail-closing historical terminalization. The shipped fix keeps the stored digest over the whole record and instead judges OCCUPANCY on identity, comparing both sides with mode_sequence stripped, so a pre-change ref converges without changing what any reader recomputes. Generation 5 changes no code: the branch had fallen 20 commits behind main and was refreshed by merge to 54e1e3c6 (never rebased, per the prohibition below), the four required checks were re-run on the merged tree, and every head-bound field in the evidence pair was re-anchored to the resulting head rather than carried forward.
